problem_summary.summary: Determine whether following next pointers from a singly linked list head eventually revisits a node.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: head, which may be null. Return a boolean. The judge supplies a ListNode with int val and ListNode next; its pos cycle-construction detail is not an argument.
constraints: pos is -1 or a valid node index

brute_force.explanation: Walk through the list while recording node identities in a HashSet. Encountering an already-seen object proves a cycle; reaching null proves termination.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A cycle makes some node identity appear twice along traversal, while an acyclic next chain visits each node at most once and ends at null.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) expected, where n is the number of distinct nodes reachable before termination or repetition.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for the set of visited node references.

optimized.explanation: Move slow by one link and fast by two. If a cycle exists, fast eventually laps slow; if fast reaches null, the list is acyclic.
optimized.correctness_idea: Inside a cycle, the gap between fast and slow changes by one node per iteration modulo the cycle length, so it must become zero. In a finite acyclic chain, the faster pointer reaches the end.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each pointer advances at most linearly before meeting or reaching null.

steps.condition: Both fast and fast.next are non-null.
steps.action: Slow advances one node and fast advances two.

steps.condition: Fast remains able to advance two links; index 3 links back to index 1.
steps.action: Advance both pointers at their respective speeds.

steps.condition: slow and fast reference the same node object.

edge_cases.case: Null head or one node with next == null
edge_cases.handling: Fast cannot advance two links, so the method returns false.
Slow and fast meet on the first advancement.
The pointers eventually meet after entering the cycle.
